key_insight: The local tangent residual (LTR) estimates whether turbulent-flow data can benefit from nonlinear compression before training an autoencoder.
engineering_relevance: LTR can help practitioners avoid costly autoencoder architecture searches and hyperparameter tuning when POD already provides sufficient compression.
method: Estimate nonlinear compression potential from local data geometry using LTR, without model training or a threshold parameter.
Quantify trained decoder nonlinearity using decoder linearisation error (DLE), comparing the decoder with a linearised surrogate.
Relate LTR and DLE to autoencoder compression performance.
evidence_signal: Across two vortex street cases and a wind-turbine turbulent wake, LTR reproduced dominant trends in autoencoder compression performance, while large LTR was corroborated by large DLE.
watch_item: Validation in the abstract is limited to three flow cases; generalisation to other turbulent-flow datasets remains to be established.
paper_title: A Priori Estimation of the Non-Linear Compression Potential and Quantification of Autoencoder Non-Linearity in Turbulent Flows
